        let Ok(mut rec) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&body) else {
            rows.push(json!({ "file": rel_file, "verdict": "parse-error" }));
            continue;
        };
        let id = rec.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let src = rec.get("src").and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_string);
        let v = br::classify(
            rec.get("name").and_then(Value::as_str),
            src.as_deref(),
            rec.get("srcText").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
            rec.get("srcDivergence").and_then(Value::as_str),
            &files,
            &read_file,
        );

        // ONLY the keys this verdict sets, matching the script's per-verdict spread: a key a branch never
        // set was ABSENT, not null, and a `--json` consumer that tells those apart would otherwise read
        // every record as confident-false.
        let mut row = json!({
            "id": id, "src": src, "file": rel_file, "verdict": v.verdict, "symbol": v.symbol,
        });
        for k in v.keys {
            let val = match *k {
                "score" => json!(v.score),
                "region" => json!(v.region),
                "by" => json!(v.by),
                "best" => json!(v.best),
                "bestScore" => json!(v.best_score),
                "runnerUp" => json!(v.runner_up),
                "runnerUpScore" => json!(v.runner_up_score),
                "confident" => json!(v.confident),
                "renamedTo" => json!(v.renamed_to),
                "reason" => json!(v.reason),
                _ => Value::Null,
            };
            row[*k] = val;
        }

        let mut write_back = false;
        if apply && (v.verdict == "stale-pointer" || v.verdict == "moved") && v.confident {
            if let Some(b) = v.best.as_ref() {
                rec["src"] = Value::String(b.clone());
                row["repointedTo"] = Value::String(b.clone());
                repointed += 1;
                write_back = true;
            }
        }
        // The file is gone and nothing in `src/` matches, so there is nothing to re-point TO. `src` goes
        // away and the path it named is preserved in `srcRetired` — nulling alone would throw away the one
        // fact a later reader needs.
        if retire
            && v.verdict == "stale-pointer"
            && !v.confident
            && src.is_some()
            && rec.get("srcRetired").is_none()
        {
            rec["srcRetired"] = Value::String(src.clone().unwrap_or_default());
            if let Some(o) = rec.as_object_mut() {
                // SHIFT, not swap. With `preserve_order` on, `Map::remove` is a SWAP-remove: it moves the
                // LAST entry into the removed slot, which put the just-appended `srcRetired` where `src`
                // had been. Functionally the same record, but a different file on disk — and every seed
                // retired before this carries `srcRetired` at the END, so a swap would leave two
                // conventions in one tree.
                o.shift_remove("src");
            }
            row["retiredFrom"] = Value::String(src.clone().unwrap_or_default());
            retired += 1;
            write_back = true;
        }
        if annotate
            && v.verdict == "drifted"
            && v.reason.is_some()
            && rec.get("srcDivergence").is_none()
        {
            rec["srcDivergence"] = Value::String(v.reason.clone().unwrap_or_default());
            row["annotated"] = Value::Bool(true);
            annotated += 1;
            write_back = true;
        }
        if write_back {
            let out = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            std::fs::write(path, format!("{out}\n"))
                .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        }
        rows.push(row);
    }

    let mut counts: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, usize> = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for r in &rows {
        *counts.entry(r["verdict"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string()).or_default() += 1;
    }

    if as_json {
        let summary = json!({
            "total": rows.len(), "counts": counts, "repointed": repointed,
            "annotated": annotated, "retired": retired,
            "applied": apply, "annotateMode": annotate,
        });
        bsc_util::emit(&serde_json::to_string_pretty(&json!({ "summary": summary, "rows": rows }))
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        return Ok(());
    }

    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
        "\nrecord↔file provenance — {} packaged records under data/components/app/**",
        rows.len()
    ));
    let mut ordered: Vec<(&String, &usize)> = counts.iter().collect();
    ordered.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(a.1));
    for (k, v) in ordered {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("  {k:<14} {v}"));
    }
    if apply {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("\n  re-pointed: {repointed}"));
    }

    let of = |verdict: &str| -> Vec<&Value> {
        rows.iter().filter(|r| r["verdict"].as_str() == Some(verdict)).collect()
    };
    let s_of = |r: &Value, k: &str| r[k].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
    // JS interpolates an absent value as the literal `null`, and these lines are read by a human deciding
    // a re-point by hand — an empty gap reads as "no runner-up name", which is a different claim.
    let j_of = |r: &Value, k: &str| r[k].as_str().unwrap_or("null").to_string();
    let n_of = |r: &Value, k: &str| r[k].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);

    let stale = of("stale-pointer");
    if !stale.is_empty() {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "\nSTALE POINTERS ({}) — src names a file that is not here:",
            stale.len()
        ));
        for r in &stale {
            let fix = if let Some(t) = r.get("repointedTo").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                format!("  ⇒ re-pointed to {t} ({})", n_of(r, "score"))
            } else if r["confident"].as_bool() == Some(true) {
                format!(
                    "  ⇒ --apply would re-point to {} ({}, runner-up {})",
                    j_of(r, "best"),
                    n_of(r, "score"),
                    n_of(r, "runnerUpScore")
                )
            } else if r["best"].is_string() && n_of(r, "score") > 0.1 {
                format!(
                    "  ⇒ WEAK/AMBIGUOUS best={} ({}) runner-up={} ({}) — decide by hand",
                    j_of(r, "best"),
                    n_of(r, "score"),
                    j_of(r, "runnerUp"),
                    n_of(r, "runnerUpScore")
                )
            } else {
                "  ⇒ NO match in src/ — the file is genuinely gone; null the pointer".to_string()
            };
            bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("  {:<30} {}\n{fix}", s_of(r, "id"), s_of(r, "src")));
        }
    }

    let moved = of("moved");
    if !moved.is_empty() {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "\nMOVED ({}) — src resolves, but the record's symbol is no longer in that file:",
            moved.len()
        ));
        for r in &moved {
            let fix = if let Some(t) = r.get("repointedTo").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                format!("  ⇒ re-pointed to {t}")
            } else if r["confident"].as_bool() == Some(true) {
                format!(
                    "  ⇒ --apply would re-point to {} ({}, runner-up {})",
                    j_of(r, "best"),
                    n_of(r, "bestScore"),
                    n_of(r, "runnerUpScore")
                )
            } else {
                format!(
                    "  ⇒ best={} ({}) runner-up={} ({}) — decide by hand",
                    j_of(r, "best"),
                    n_of(r, "bestScore"),
                    j_of(r, "runnerUp"),
                    n_of(r, "runnerUpScore")
                )
            };
            let sym = r["symbol"].as_str().unwrap_or("?");
            bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                "  {:<30} {sym} not in {}\n{fix}",
                s_of(r, "id"),
                s_of(r, "src")
            ));
        }
    }

    let mut drifted = of("drifted");
    if !drifted.is_empty() {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "\nDRIFTED ({}) — src resolves, but the record is not what the file holds:",
            drifted.len()
        ));
        drifted.sort_by(|a, b| {
            let k = |r: &Value| r["region"].as_f64().unwrap_or_else(|| r["score"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0));
            k(a).partial_cmp(&k(b)).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
        });
        for r in &drifted {
            let region = r["region"].as_f64().map(|v| v.to_string()).unwrap_or("?".to_string());
            bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                "  region={region:<6} {:<30} {}  {}",
                s_of(r, "id"),
                if r["reason"].is_string() { "explained" } else { "NEEDS VERDICT" },
                s_of(r, "src")
            ));
        }
        let explained = drifted.iter().filter(|r| r["reason"].is_string()).count();
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "\n  {explained} EXPLAINED — preview parameterization, evidenced per record. `--annotate` writes"
        ));
        bsc_util::emit_line(
            "  the reason to `srcDivergence`, which moves them to the `intentional` verdict.",
        );
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "  {} NOT explained — each needs a human verdict. Refresh is the EXCEPTION:",
            drifted.len() - explained
        ));
        bsc_util::emit_line("  the record is frequently the RICHER copy.");
    }
    bsc_util::emit_line("");
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui promote-seed [--apply] …` — promote a live store record into the PACKAGED SEED, the step that
/// makes its file retirable. Ports `scripts/promote-records.mjs`, which it replaces.
fn cmd_promote_seed(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    use serde_json::Value;
    let apply = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--apply");
    let adopt_seed = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--adopt-seed");
    let only = flag_after(args, "--only");
    let limit: usize = flag_after(args, "--limit")
        .map(|v| v.parse().map_err(|_| format!("--limit '{v}' is not a number")))
        .transpose()?
        .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
    // Per-id and explicit, so a drop is reviewable in the command that caused it — never a blanket flag.
    let allow_drop: std::collections::HashSet<String> = flag_after(args, "--allow-drop")
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .split(',')
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
        .map(str::to_string)
        .collect();
    let dir = flag_after(args, "--dir");
    let repo = flag_after(args, "--repo")
        .map(std::path::PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or(std::env::current_dir().map_err(|e| format!("cannot resolve cwd: {e}"))?);

    let algos_path = repo.join("src-tauri/data/knowledge/algorithms.json");
    let mut algorithms: Value = serde_json::from_str(
        &std::fs::read_to_string(&algos_path).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read the algorithms seed: {e}"))?,
    )
    .map_err(|e| format!("the algorithms seed is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;

    // BOTH STORES, read directly — the script took two dumped JSON files.
    let store = bsc_component::cli::open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let components: Vec<Value> = store
        .list()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|b| serde_json::from_str::<Value>(b).ok())
        .collect();
    let impls: Vec<Value> = bsc_graph::implementations();

    // spec → the record that answers it. A COMPONENT wins over an impl for the same specifier.
    let mut by_spec: std::collections::HashMap<String, (&'static str, Value)> =
        std::collections::HashMap::new();
    for c in &components {
        let sp = c.get("provides").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").trim();
        let src = c.get("srcText").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
        if !sp.is_empty() && !src.trim().is_empty() {
            by_spec.insert(sp.to_string(), ("component", c.clone()));
        }
    }
    for i in &impls {
        let sp = i.get("provides").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").trim();
        let code = i.get("code").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
        if !sp.is_empty() && !code.trim().is_empty() && !by_spec.contains_key(sp) {
            by_spec.insert(sp.to_string(), ("impl", i.clone()));
        }
    }

    // The packaged seed: which specifiers it provides, which ids it uses, and where each id's JSON sits.
    // `SEED_COMPONENTS` globs the tree FLAT and keys by id, so a record's identity is its id and NOT
    // where the file sits — which is why an adoption must find the existing seed BY ID rather than at a
    // path derived from `folder`, a field that can and does disagree with reality.
    let (mut seeded_specs, mut seed_ids, mut seed_path_by_id) = (
        std::collections::HashSet::<String>::new(),
        std::collections::HashSet::<String>::new(),
        std::collections::HashMap::<String, std::path::PathBuf>::new(),
    );
    fn walk_seed(
        dir: &std::path::Path,
        specs: &mut std::collections::HashSet<String>,
        ids: &mut std::collections::HashSet<String>,
        paths: &mut std::collections::HashMap<String, std::path::PathBuf>,
        under_app: bool,
    ) {
        let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else { return };
        let mut list: Vec<std::path::PathBuf> = entries.flatten().map(|e| e.path()).collect();
        list.sort();
        for p in list {
            if p.is_dir() {
                walk_seed(&p, specs, ids, paths, under_app);
                continue;
            }
            if p.extension().and_then(|x| x.to_str()) != Some("json")
                || std::fs::metadata(&p).map(|m| m.len() > 4_000_000).unwrap_or(true)
            {
                continue;
            }
            let Ok(body) = std::fs::read_to_string(&p) else { continue };
            let Ok(r) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&body) else { continue };
            if let Some(sp) = r.get("provides").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
                specs.insert(sp.trim().to_string());
            }
            if under_app {
                if let Some(id) = r.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
                    ids.insert(id.to_string());
                    paths.entry(id.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| p.clone());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    walk_seed(
        &repo.join("src-tauri/data/components"),
        &mut seeded_specs,
        &mut std::collections::HashSet::new(),
        &mut std::collections::HashMap::new(),
        false,
    );
    walk_seed(
        &repo.join("src-tauri/data/components/app"),
        &mut std::collections::HashSet::new(),
        &mut seed_ids,
        &mut seed_path_by_id,
        true,
    );
    for im in algorithms.get("implementations").and_then(Value::as_array).into_iter().flatten() {
        if let Some(sp) = im.get("provides").and_then(Value::as_str) {
            seeded_specs.insert(sp.trim().to_string());
        }
    }

    // THE PACKAGED SEED COUNTS toward resolvability. `emit-records` materializes the SEED — never the
    // store — into `.bsc-records/`, so a specifier the seed provides is precisely what the bundle will
    // resolve. Building this from the registry and the STORE alone made every module whose file had been
    // retired in favour of a seed record read as unresolvable.
    let registered: std::collections::HashSet<String> =
        std::fs::read_to_string(repo.join("src-tauri/data/ui/platform-modules.json"))
            .ok()
            .and_then(|b| serde_json::from_str::<Vec<String>>(&b).ok())
            .unwrap_or_default()
            .into_iter()
            .collect();
    let mut resolvable: std::collections::HashSet<String> = registered.clone();
    resolvable.extend(seeded_specs.iter().cloned());
    resolvable.extend(by_spec.keys().cloned());
    for c in &components {
        if let Some(id) = c.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) {
            resolvable.insert(format!("@/components/{id}"));
        }
    }

    // Read from the SOURCE rather than imported, and it FAILS CLOSED: if the catalogue ever stops listing
    // entries literally this is empty, and every app screen stays skipped — the safe direction.
    let catalogued: std::collections::HashSet<String> = {
        let re = regex::Regex::new(r#"pageId:\s*"([^"]+)""#).expect("pageId");
        std::fs::read_to_string(repo.join("src/app/runtime/shadowPages.ts"))
            .map(|b| re.captures_iter(&b).map(|c| c[1].to_string()).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default()
    };

    let src_files = crate::retirable::list_src(&repo);
    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct Promotable {
        file: String,
        spec: String,
        rec: Value,
    }
    let (mut promote_component, mut promote_impl) =
        (Vec::<Promotable>::new(), Vec::<Promotable>::new());
    let mut body_differs: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut build_time_only: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut page_record: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut unresolvable: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut uncompilable: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut unclosed_composes: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let (mut already_seeded_n, mut no_record_n) = (0usize, 0usize);

    for file in src_files.iter().filter(|f| crate::promote::is_module(f)) {
        if only.as_ref().is_some_and(|o| o != file) {
            continue;
        }
        let spec = crate::promote::spec_of(file);
        let hit = by_spec.get(&spec);
        let file_src = hit
            .map(|_| {
                bsc_record::record_source::file_as_record_source(
                    &repo.join("src").join(file),
                    file,
                )
                .unwrap_or_default()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let view = hit.map(|(kind, rec)| crate::promote::RecordView {
            id: rec.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
            kind,
            role: rec.get("role").and_then(Value::as_str),
            page_kind: rec.get("pageKind").and_then(Value::as_str),
            source: rec
                .get("srcText")
                .or_else(|| rec.get("code"))
                .and_then(Value::as_str)
                .unwrap_or(""),
        });
        let verdict = crate::promote::classify(
            seeded_specs.contains(&spec),
            view.as_ref(),
            &file_src,
            &|id| catalogued.contains(id),
            &|s| resolvable.contains(s),
            &bsc_record::record_source::runtime_imports,
        );
        match verdict {
            Err(crate::promote::Skip::AlreadySeeded) => already_seeded_n += 1,
            Err(crate::promote::Skip::NoRecord) => no_record_n += 1,
            Err(crate::promote::Skip::BuildTimeOnly) => build_time_only.push(file.clone()),
            Err(crate::promote::Skip::PageNotCatalogued(id)) => {
                page_record.push(format!("{file} — catalogue `{id}` in SHADOW_PAGES first"));
            }
            Err(crate::promote::Skip::Unresolvable(specs)) => {
                unresolvable.push(format!(
                    "{file} — needs {}",
                    specs.iter().take(3).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
                ));
            }
            Err(crate::promote::Skip::BodyDiffers { record_len, file_len, delta }) => {
                body_differs.push(format!(
                    "{file} — record {record_len} vs file {file_len} chars ({}{delta})",
                    if delta >= 0 { "+" } else { "" }
                ));
            }
            Ok(()) => {
                if promote_component.len() + promote_impl.len() >= limit {
                    break;
                }
                let (kind, rec) = hit.expect("Ok implies a record");
                let p = Promotable { file: file.clone(), spec, rec: rec.clone() };
                if *kind == "component" { promote_component.push(p) } else { promote_impl.push(p) }
            }
        }
    }

    // FIXED POINT. Resolvability has to be judged against what the PACKAGE will hold once this run lands
    // — registry ∪ already-seeded ∪ promoted-here — not against the live store, which knows records that
    // will still be missing from the shipped seed afterwards. That is circular (whether A is promotable
    // depends on whether B is), so it is settled by iterating until nothing more drops. It also covers
    // BARE specifiers, not just `@/…`: `platformBoundary` checks those too, and `detachedtabstrip` failed
    // on `@tauri-apps/api/window` after an earlier pass that only looked at `@/`.
    let imports_of = |src: &str| -> Vec<String> {
        bsc_record::record_source::runtime_imports(src)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|s| !s.starts_with("./") && !s.starts_with("../"))
            .filter(|s| crate::promote::needs_resolution(s))
            .collect()
    };
    for _ in 0..20 {
        let mut will_exist: std::collections::HashSet<String> = registered.clone();
        will_exist.extend(seeded_specs.iter().cloned());
        for p in promote_component.iter().chain(promote_impl.iter()) {
            will_exist.insert(p.spec.clone());
            if let Some(id) = p.rec.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                will_exist.insert(format!("@/components/{id}"));
            }
        }
        let mut dropped = 0usize;
        for list in [&mut promote_component, &mut promote_impl] {
            list.retain(|p| {
                let src = p
                    .rec
                    .get("srcText")
                    .or_else(|| p.rec.get("code"))
                    .and_then(Value::as_str)
                    .unwrap_or("");
                let missing: Vec<String> =
                    imports_of(src).into_iter().filter(|s| !will_exist.contains(s)).collect();
                if missing.is_empty() {
                    return true;
                }
                dropped += 1;
                unresolvable.push(format!(
                    "{} — needs {}",
                    p.file,
                    missing.iter().take(3).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
                ));
                false
            });
        }
        if dropped == 0 {
            break;
        }
    }

    // DOES IT COMPILE AS TSX? The runtime loader compiles every record with esbuild's **tsx** loader, and
    // TSX is not a superset of TS: `<T>(x) => x` is a generic arrow in a `.ts` file and an unclosed JSX
    // element in a `.tsx` one. So a module `tsc` and Vite accept all day can be uncompilable AS A RECORD —
    // `deployEnv.ts` is exactly that, and it slips every gate above because its record matches its file
    // perfectly.
    //
    // Batched through ONE esbuild invocation rather than N: each is ~300ms of process start, and the whole
    // set compiles in well under a second together. esbuild names every file it could not build.
    if !promote_component.is_empty() || !promote_impl.is_empty() {
        let tmp = repo.join(".promote-compile-check");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&tmp);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&tmp).map_err(|e| format!("compile check: {e}"))?;
        let all: Vec<Promotable> =
            promote_component.iter().chain(promote_impl.iter()).cloned().collect();
        for (i, p) in all.iter().enumerate() {
            let src = p.rec.get("srcText").or_else(|| p.rec.get("code")).and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
            let _ = std::fs::write(tmp.join(format!("m{i:04}.tsx")), src);
        }
        let out = std::process::Command::new("npx")
            .args([
                "esbuild",
                &format!("{}/*.tsx", tmp.display()),
                "--loader:.tsx=tsx",
                "--format=cjs",
                &format!("--outdir={}/out", tmp.display()),
            ])
            .current_dir(&repo)
            .output();
        match out {
            Ok(o) => {
                let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stderr);
                let re = regex::Regex::new(r"m(\d{4})\.tsx").expect("compile names");
                let broken: std::collections::HashSet<usize> = re
                    .captures_iter(&stderr)
                    .filter_map(|c| c[1].parse::<usize>().ok())
                    .collect();
                if !broken.is_empty() {
                    for (i, p) in all.iter().enumerate() {
                        if broken.contains(&i) {
                            uncompilable.push(format!("{} — does not compile as TSX", p.file));
                        }
                    }
                    let bad: std::collections::HashSet<String> = all
                        .iter()
                        .enumerate()
                        .filter(|(i, _)| broken.contains(i))
                        .map(|(_, p)| p.file.clone())
                        .collect();
                    promote_component.retain(|p| !bad.contains(&p.file));
                    promote_impl.retain(|p| !bad.contains(&p.file));
                }
            }
            // A MISSING esbuild is REPORTED, never silently treated as "everything compiles" — that would
            // turn the one gate no other check can stand in for into a no-op.
            Err(e) => bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                "   WARNING: the TSX compile check could not run ({e}) — `npx esbuild` is required; \
                 every record below is UNVERIFIED for TSX compilability"
            )),
        }
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&tmp);
    }

    // DOES ITS `composes` CLOSE? An impl names the impls it builds on, and `knowledge.test.ts` asserts
    // every one is a REAL impl in the seed — so promoting an impl whose `composes` points at something
    // still store-only breaks the seed the moment it lands.
    let impl_by_id: std::collections::HashMap<String, Value> = impls
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|i| Some((i.get("id")?.as_str()?.to_string(), i.clone())))
        .collect();
    let rec_by_id: std::collections::HashMap<String, Value> = {
        let mut m = impl_by_id.clone();
        for c in &components {
            if let Some(id) = c.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                m.entry(id.to_string()).or_insert_with(|| c.clone());
            }
        }
        m
    };
    let composes_of = |v: &Value| -> Vec<String> {
        v.get("composes")
            .and_then(Value::as_array)
            .map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|x| x.as_str().map(str::to_string)).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default()
    };
    let carry_for = |promote_impl: &[Promotable]| -> Vec<Value> {
        let mut seeded: std::collections::HashSet<String> = algorithms
            .get("implementations")
            .and_then(Value::as_array)
            .into_iter()
            .flatten()
            .filter_map(|i| i.get("id")?.as_str().map(str::to_string))
            .collect();
        for p in promote_impl {
            if let Some(id) = p.rec.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                seeded.insert(id.to_string());
            }
        }
        let by_id: std::collections::HashMap<String, crate::graph_closure::Rec> = impl_by_id
            .iter()
            .map(|(k, v)| {
                (
                    k.clone(),
                    crate::graph_closure::Rec {
                        provides: v.get("provides").and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_string),
                        composes: composes_of(v),
                    },
                )
            })
            .collect();
        let roots: Vec<String> = promote_impl
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|p| composes_of(&p.rec))
            .filter(|c| !seeded.contains(c))
            .collect();
        crate::graph_closure::library_carry_closure(&roots, &by_id, &seeded)
            .carry
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|id| impl_by_id.get(&id).cloned())
            .collect()
    };
    let carried = carry_for(&promote_impl);

    {
        let mut impl_ids: std::collections::HashSet<String> = algorithms
            .get("implementations")
            .and_then(Value::as_array)
            .into_iter()
            .flatten()
            .filter_map(|i| i.get("id")?.as_str().map(str::to_string))
            .collect();
        for p in &promote_impl {
            if let Some(id) = p.rec.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                impl_ids.insert(id.to_string());
            }
        }
        for c in &carried {
            if let Some(id) = c.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                impl_ids.insert(id.to_string());
            }
        }
        // A COMPOSED id whose module is already RESOLVABLE closes the closure just as well as a seeded
        // impl. The narrower question — "is this composed id a seeded impl?" — can never be satisfied by
        // a permanently-file module: 7 of 34 blocking ids are `import.meta.glob` modules that CANNOT be
        // records at all, so every record composing one was held forever on a condition it could not meet.
        let spec_for_composed = |id: &str| -> Option<String> {
            let rec = rec_by_id.get(id)?;
            if let Some(p) = rec.get("provides").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                if p.starts_with("@/") {
                    return Some(p.trim().to_string());
                }
            }
            let src = rec.get("src").and_then(Value::as_str)?.replace('\\', "/");
            let stem = src.strip_prefix("src/").unwrap_or(&src);
            let stem = [".tsx", ".ts"].iter().find_map(|e| stem.strip_suffix(*e)).unwrap_or(stem);
            Some(format!("@/{}", stem.strip_suffix("/index").unwrap_or(stem)))
        };
        let closed_by_resolution = |id: &str| -> bool {
            seeded_specs.contains(id)
                || spec_for_composed(id).is_some_and(|s| resolvable.contains(&s))
        };
        // A FIXPOINT, not one pass: dropping an impl can dangle another that composed it.
        loop {
            let mut settled = true;
            let mut keep: Vec<Promotable> = Vec::new();
            for p in &promote_impl {
                let missing: Vec<String> = composes_of(&p.rec)
                    .into_iter()
                    .filter(|c| !impl_ids.contains(c) && !closed_by_resolution(c))
                    .collect();
                if missing.is_empty() {
                    keep.push(p.clone());
                    continue;
                }
                unclosed_composes.push(format!(
                    "{} — composes {}",
                    p.file,
                    missing.iter().take(3).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
                ));
                if let Some(id) = p.rec.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                    impl_ids.remove(id);
                }
                settled = false;
            }
            promote_impl = keep;
            if settled {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    // Recompute the carry from what SURVIVED: the fixed point can drop an impl for an unrelated reason,
    // and a library record carried only for that impl would be seeded with nothing referencing it.
    let carried_kept = carry_for(&promote_impl);

    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
        "promotable: {} component(s) + {} impl(s){}",
        promote_component.len(),
        promote_impl.len(),
        if carried_kept.is_empty() {
            String::new()
        } else {
            format!(" (+ {} library record(s) carried to close their composes)", carried_kept.len())
        }
    ));
    for c in &carried_kept {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "   carry: {}{}",
            c.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
            if c.get("role").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("primitive") {
                "  [language primitive]"
            } else {
                ""
            }
        ));
    }
    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
        "skipped — already seeded {already_seeded_n}, no record {no_record_n}, body differs {}, \
         build-time-only {}, role:page {}, unresolvable {}, uncompilable {}, unclosed-composes {}",
        body_differs.len(),
        build_time_only.len(),
        page_record.len(),
        unresolvable.len(),
        uncompilable.len(),
        unclosed_composes.len()
    ));
    for f in &body_differs {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   body differs: {f}"));
    }
    for f in &build_time_only {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   import.meta.glob: {f}"));
    }
    for f in &page_record {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   role:page (catalogue it in shadowPages first): {f}"));
    }
    for f in &unresolvable {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   unresolvable import: {f}"));
    }
    for f in &uncompilable {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   {f}"));
    }
    for f in &unclosed_composes {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   unclosed composes: {f}"));
    }
    // NAME what will be promoted, not just how many — a bare count forced the operator to `--apply` in
    // order to find out what `--apply` would do, the single thing a dry run exists to avoid.
    for r in &promote_component {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   + component {}", r.file));
    }
    for r in &promote_impl {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   + impl      {}", r.file));
    }

    if !apply {
        bsc_util::emit_line("\n(dry run — pass --apply to write)");
        return Ok(());
    }

    let (mut skipped_at_write, mut adopted) = (0usize, 0usize);
    for p in &promote_component {
        let rec = &p.rec;
        let id = rec.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let folder = rec.get("folder").and_then(Value::as_str).filter(|f| !f.is_empty()).unwrap_or("misc");
        let existing = seed_path_by_id.get(&id).cloned();
        let path = existing.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {
            repo.join("src-tauri/data/components/app").join(folder).join(format!("{id}.json"))
        });

        // NEVER overwrite an existing seed — seven curated seeds were clobbered before this guard.
        // `--adopt-seed` is the ONE narrow exception, and it inverts the case the guard was written for:
        // there the seed is the worse copy, BEHIND the file while the store record IS the file, which the
        // gate above has already proven.
        let mut adopting = false;
        if path.is_file() {
            let seed_rec: Value = serde_json::from_str(
                &std::fs::read_to_string(&path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?,
            )
            .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
            let file_src = bsc_record::record_source::file_as_record_source(
                &repo.join("src").join(&p.file),
                &p.file,
            )
            .unwrap_or_default();
            let a = bsc_record::record_source::seed_adoption(
                seed_rec.get("srcText").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
                seed_rec.get("provides").and_then(Value::as_str),
                rec.get("srcText").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
                rec.get("provides").and_then(Value::as_str),
                &file_src,
            );
            if !adopt_seed {
                bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                    "   SKIPPED (a seed already occupies that path): {} → {id}.json{}",
                    p.file,
                    if a.verdict == "adopt" { " — it is STALE; --adopt-seed replaces it" } else { "" }
                ));
                skipped_at_write += 1;
                continue;
            }
            // The export-loss refusal is the ONE `--allow-drop` can override, and only for a record named
            // on the command line — `lost` being non-empty is what identifies it, so the flag cannot
            // become a blanket "write anyway".
            let overriding = a.verdict == "refuse" && !a.lost.is_empty() && allow_drop.contains(&id);
            if a.verdict != "adopt" && !overriding {
                bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                    "   {} ({}): {id}",
                    if a.verdict == "keep" { "kept" } else { "REFUSED" },
                    a.reason
                ));
                skipped_at_write += 1;
                continue;
            }
            if overriding {
                bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                    "   ADOPTED DESPITE dropping {} (--allow-drop): {id}",
                    a.lost.join(", ")
                ));
            }
            bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                "   adopted the store record over a stale seed: {id}  ({})",
                a.reason
            ));
            adopted += 1;
            adopting = true;
        }
        // AND the id must be free ANYWHERE in the seed, not just at this path: `SEED_COMPONENTS` is a
        // flat glob, so the same id under a DIFFERENT folder sails past a path check — which is what
        // happened, leaving two records with one id and `reconcileSeed` re-pushing it every boot.
        if !adopting && seed_ids.contains(&id) {
            bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                "   SKIPPED (that id is already in the seed elsewhere): {} → {id}",
                p.file
            ));
            skipped_at_write += 1;
            continue;
        }
        seed_ids.insert(id.clone());
        let out = crate::promote::project(rec, &crate::promote::SEED_FIELDS);
        if let Some(d) = path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(d).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", d.display()))?;
        }
        let body = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        std::fs::write(&path, format!("{body}\n")).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    }

    // IMPLS — appended to the one algorithms document, sorted by id so the file stays reviewable and a
    // re-run produces the same bytes.
    if !promote_impl.is_empty() || !carried_kept.is_empty() {
        let list = algorithms
            .get_mut("implementations")
            .and_then(Value::as_array_mut)
            .ok_or("the algorithms seed has no implementations[]")?;
        let mut at_by_id: std::collections::HashMap<String, usize> = list
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter_map(|(i, e)| Some((e.get("id")?.as_str()?.to_string(), i)))
            .collect();
        let writing: Vec<Value> =
            carried_kept.iter().cloned().chain(promote_impl.iter().map(|p| p.rec.clone())).collect();
        // Every id that WILL be an impl once this run finishes — `composes` is filtered against it.
        let mut will_be_impl: std::collections::HashSet<String> =
            list.iter().filter_map(|e| e.get("id")?.as_str().map(str::to_string)).collect();
        for r in &writing {
            if let Some(id) = r.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                will_be_impl.insert(id.to_string());
            }
        }
        for rec in &writing {
            let mut entry = crate::promote::project(rec, &crate::promote::IMPL_KEEP);
            let id = entry.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
            let composes: Vec<String> = entry
                .get("composes")
                .and_then(Value::as_array)
                .map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|x| x.as_str().map(str::to_string)).collect())
                .unwrap_or_default();
            // DROP a composes target that is not an impl: `composes` models an edge in the ALGORITHM
            // graph, so a target that is a registered platform module or a component record is not an
            // edge it can express — and writing one produces a DANGLING reference the seed's own
            // integrity guard rejects. Dropping is not losing the dependency: the record still IMPORTS
            // the module and resolves it through the registry. Only the edge goes, and it never existed.
            let (keep, dropped): (Vec<String>, Vec<String>) =
                composes.into_iter().partition(|c| will_be_impl.contains(c));
            if !dropped.is_empty() {
                bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                    "   {id}: dropped {} non-impl composes target(s) — {}",
                    dropped.len(),
                    dropped.iter().take(3).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
                ));
            }
            entry["composes"] = Value::Array(keep.into_iter().map(Value::String).collect());

            // NEVER APPEND A DUPLICATE ID. An id comes from the FILE STEM, so promoting
            // `…/examples/sort.ts` once appended a SECOND `sort.ts` beside a curated one.
            if let Some(at) = at_by_id.get(&id).copied() {
                if !adopt_seed {
                    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                        "   SKIPPED (that impl id is already in the seed): {id}"
                    ));
                    skipped_at_write += 1;
                    continue;
                }
                bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                    "   replaced the seeded impl with the promoted module: {id}"
                ));
                list[at] = entry;
                continue;
            }
            at_by_id.insert(id, list.len());
            list.push(entry);
        }
        list.sort_by(|a, b| {
            a.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("")
                .cmp(b.get("id").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""))
        });
        std::fs::write(&algos_path, crate::refresh_seed::serialize_algorithms(&algorithms)?)
            .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", algos_path.display()))?;
    }

    // COUNT WHAT LANDED, NOT WHAT WAS PLANNED. This used to print the size of the promote list — the
    // number taken BEFORE the never-overwrite guard runs — so a run that wrote 43 reported 49. A tool
    // that overstates its own output is worse than one that does nothing, because the next step trusts it.
    let landed = promote_component.len() + promote_impl.len() - skipped_at_write.min(promote_component.len() + promote_impl.len());
    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
        "\npromoted {landed} record(s) into the seed{}{}",
        if adopted > 0 { format!(", {adopted} of them ADOPTED over a stale seed") } else { String::new() },
        if skipped_at_write > 0 {
            format!(" ({skipped_at_write} declined — a seed already occupied the path)")
        } else {
            String::new()
        }
    ));
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui refresh-seed [--apply] [--only <src-path>]` — the drifted-seed sweep. Ports
/// `scripts/refresh-drifted-seeds.mjs`, which it replaces. The `--store`/`--impls` JSON dumps the script
/// took are gone: this reads both stores directly.
fn cmd_refresh_seed(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let apply = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--apply");
    let only = flag_after(args, "--only");
    let dir = flag_after(args, "--dir");
    let repo = flag_after(args, "--repo")
        .map(std::path::PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or(std::env::current_dir().map_err(|e| format!("cannot resolve cwd: {e}"))?);

    let src_files = crate::retirable::list_src(&repo);
    let (seeds, algos) = crate::refresh_seed::collect(&repo);

    // Every `@/…` a RECORD may import: a registered platform module, or a specifier some record
    // provides. Mirrors what `platformBoundary.test.ts` asserts.
    let mut resolvable: std::collections::HashSet<String> =
        std::fs::read_to_string(repo.join("src-tauri/data/ui/platform-modules.json"))
            .ok()
            .and_then(|b| serde_json::from_str::<Vec<String>>(&b).ok())
            .unwrap_or_default()
            .into_iter()
            .collect();
    for s in &seeds {
        resolvable.insert(s.spec.clone());
        resolvable.insert(format!("@/components/{}", s.id));
    }

    // The import index, over BOTH the packaged records and `src/`.
    let mut sources: Vec<(String, String)> =
        seeds.iter().map(|s| (format!("record:{}", s.id), s.source.clone())).collect();
    for f in &src_files {
        if f.ends_with(".ts") || f.ends_with(".tsx") {
            if let Ok(b) = std::fs::read_to_string(repo.join("src").join(f)) {
                sources.push((f.clone(), b));
            }
        }
    }
    let index = crate::refresh_seed::import_index(&sources);

    // The LIVE copies — the "has anyone edited this record" gate. An impl store that cannot be read
    // leaves impls unconsidered rather than refreshed blind.
    let store = bsc_component::cli::open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let live_component = |id: &str| -> Option<String> {
        store.get(id).ok().flatten().and_then(|b| {
            serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&b)
                .ok()?
                .get("srcText")?
                .as_str()
                .map(str::to_string)
        })
    };
    let mut live_impl: std::collections::HashMap<String, String> = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    for im in bsc_graph::implementations() {
        if let (Some(id), Some(code)) = (
            im.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str),
            im.get("code").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str),
        ) {
            live_impl.insert(id.to_string(), code.to_string());
        }
    }

    let (mut refreshed, mut already_ok) = (0usize, 0usize);
    let (mut edited, mut breaking, mut unresolvable) =
        (Vec::<String>::new(), Vec::<String>::new(), Vec::<String>::new());
    let mut algos = algos;
    let mut algos_dirty = false;

    for seed in &seeds {
        let Some(file) = crate::refresh_seed::file_for(&seed.spec, &src_files) else { continue };
        if only.as_ref().is_some_and(|o| *o != file) {
            continue;
        }
        // The file's source as a RECORD states its imports absolutely, so every comparison below asks
        // about the form the record would actually hold rather than the form on disk.
        let Ok(file_src) =
            bsc_record::record_source::file_as_record_source(&repo.join("src").join(&file), &file)
        else {
            continue;
        };
        let live = if seed.kind == "impl" {
            live_impl.get(&seed.id).cloned()
        } else {
            live_component(&seed.id)
        };
        let empty: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        let consumers_of = |n: &str| {
            index.get(&seed.spec).and_then(|m| m.get(n)).unwrap_or(&empty).clone()
        };
        let is_resolvable = |s: &str| resolvable.contains(s);

        match crate::refresh_seed::decide(
            &seed.source,
            &file_src,
            live.as_deref(),
            &consumers_of,
            &is_resolvable,
        ) {
            crate::refresh_seed::Verdict::AlreadyOk => already_ok += 1,
            crate::refresh_seed::Verdict::Edited => edited.push(file.clone()),
            crate::refresh_seed::Verdict::WouldDropExport { lost, consumers } => {
                breaking.push(format!(
                    "{file} — would drop {} (imported by {})",
                    lost.join(", "),
                    consumers.iter().take(3).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
                ));
            }
            crate::refresh_seed::Verdict::Unresolvable(specs) => {
                unresolvable.push(format!(
                    "{file} — imports {}, which no record provides and the platform does not register",
                    specs.iter().take(3).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
                ));
            }
            crate::refresh_seed::Verdict::Refresh { next, preamble_lines } => {
                refreshed += 1;
                bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                    "   {}  [{}] {file}  ({} → {} chars, preamble {})",
                    if apply { "refreshed" } else { "would refresh" },
                    seed.kind,
                    bsc_record::record_source::norm(&seed.source).chars().count(),
                    next.trim_end().chars().count(),
                    if preamble_lines > 0 {
                        format!("{preamble_lines} lines kept")
                    } else {
                        "none".to_string()
                    }
                ));
                if !apply {
                    continue;
                }
                if seed.kind == "impl" {
                    // Mutated in memory and the whole document flushed ONCE after the sweep — writing
                    // per record would rewrite 6.6 MB N times and leave it half-updated if one threw.
                    if let Some(list) = algos
                        .as_mut()
                        .and_then(|a| a.get_mut("implementations"))
                        .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array_mut)
                    {
                        if let Some(im) = list.iter_mut().find(|im| {
                            im.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(&seed.id)
                        }) {
                            im["code"] = serde_json::Value::String(next);
                            algos_dirty = true;
                        }
                    }
                } else if let Some(p) = seed.path.as_ref() {
                    let mut rec: serde_json::Value =
                        serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(p).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)
                            .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", p.display()))?;
                    rec["srcText"] = serde_json::Value::String(next);
                    let body = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                    std::fs::write(p, format!("{body}\n")).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if apply && algos_dirty {
        if let Some(a) = algos.as_ref() {
            std::fs::write(
                repo.join("src-tauri/data/knowledge/algorithms.json"),
                crate::refresh_seed::serialize_algorithms(a)?,
            )
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        }
    }

    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("\nseeds already matching the file: {already_ok}"));
    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
        "{}:                {refreshed}",
        if apply { "refreshed" } else { "would refresh" }
    ));
    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("SKIPPED — the record was edited:  {}", edited.len()));
    for f in &edited {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   {f}"));
    }
    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("SKIPPED — would drop a used export: {}", breaking.len()));
    for f in &breaking {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   {f}"));
    }
    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
        "SKIPPED — a record cannot resolve its imports: {}",
        unresolvable.len()
    ));
    for f in &unresolvable {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   {f}"));
    }
    if !apply {
        bsc_util::emit_line("\n(dry run — pass --apply to write)");
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui lift <src-relative-path>… [--apply] [--new-record]` — the module reshape. Ports
/// `scripts/lift-component-module.mjs`, which it replaces.
fn cmd_lift(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    const USAGE: &str = "usage: bsc ui lift <src-relative-path>… [--apply] [--new-record] [--repo <dir>]";
    let apply = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--apply");
    let force_new = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--new-record");
    let dir = flag_after(args, "--dir");
    let repo = flag_after(args, "--repo")
        .map(std::path::PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or(std::env::current_dir().map_err(|e| format!("cannot resolve cwd: {e}"))?);
    let by = flag_after(args, "--by");

    let mut targets: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--repo" | "--dir" | "--by" => {
                it.next();
            }
            other if other.starts_with("--") => {}
            other => targets.push(other.to_string()),
        }
    }
    if targets.is_empty() {
        return Err(USAGE.into());
    }

    let store = bsc_component::cli::open_component_store(&dir)?;
    // Every component record, and the `src` it was lifted from. A LIST per file, not one record: a file
    // with several exported components has several records pointing at it, and keying by `src` silently
    // kept whichever came last — which made the choice of which record becomes THE MODULE arbitrary.
    let all: Vec<serde_json::Value> = store
        .list()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|b| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(b).ok())
        .collect();
    let norm = |s: &str| s.replace('\\', "/");
    let all_ids: Vec<(String, String)> = all
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|c| {
            let id = c.get("id")?.as_str()?.to_string();
            let src = c.get("src").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(norm).unwrap_or_default();
            Some((id, src))
        })
        .collect();

    let (mut lifted, mut skipped) = (0usize, Vec::<String>::new());
    for rel in &targets {
        let rel_clean = rel.trim_start_matches("./").to_string();
        let src_rel =
            if rel_clean.starts_with("src/") { rel_clean.clone() } else { format!("src/{rel_clean}") };
        let abs = repo.join(&src_rel);
        let records: Vec<String> =
            all_ids.iter().filter(|(_, s)| *s == src_rel).map(|(id, _)| id.clone()).collect();

        // The harvest is only consulted once the cheap refusals have passed — it parses the file.
        let cand = if abs.is_file() && !records.is_empty() {
            bsc_graph::extract::harvest_module(&abs, &repo)
        } else {
            None
        };
        let cand_ref = cand
            .as_ref()
            .map(|c| (c.code.as_str(), c.module_state.as_slice(), c.provides.as_deref()));

        let plan = match crate::lift::plan(
            &rel_clean,
            abs.is_file(),
            &records,
            &all_ids,
            force_new,
            cand_ref,
        ) {
            Ok(p) => p,
            Err(skip) => {
                skipped.push(format!("{rel} — {}", skip.reason()));
                continue;
            }
        };
        let c = cand.as_ref().expect("a plan implies a candidate");
        let provides = c.provides.as_deref().unwrap_or_default();

        let how = if plan.new_record {
            format!("NEW record {}", plan.module_id)
        } else {
            plan.module_id.clone()
        };
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "  {} {how:<34} {provides}",
            if apply { "lift" } else { "would lift" }
        ));
        if !apply {
            lifted += 1;
            continue;
        }

        // A REFUSED WRITE IS A FINDING, NOT A CRASH. The store runs its own gates, and letting one throw
        // killed a 40-item batch on its first refusal and lost the other 39. Each target is caught here.
        let wrote = (|| -> Result<(), String> {
            if plan.new_record {
                // `role: composite`, never `page` — a module record is the FILE, and the store's page
                // gate rightly refuses a page that cannot render standalone. The per-component records
                // keep their own roles; this one only has to answer the specifier.
                let folder = all
                    .iter()
                    .find(|c| c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(&records[0]))
                    .and_then(|c| c.get("folder").cloned())
                    .unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);
                let mut rec = serde_json::json!({
                    "id": plan.module_id, "name": plan.module_id, "kitId": "base-studio-code",
                    "role": "composite", "provides": provides, "src": src_rel,
                    "srcText": "export {};\n",
                });
                if !folder.is_null() {
                    rec["folder"] = folder;
                }
                bsc_component::cli::apply_lift(
                    &store,
                    &[rec],
                    by.as_deref(),
                    "module record: this file is also a module, beside its component records",
                )?;
                bsc_component::cli::replace_src(&store, &plan.module_id, &c.code, by.as_deref())
            } else {
                bsc_component::cli::replace_src(&store, &plan.module_id, &c.code, by.as_deref())?;
                bsc_component::cli::apply_lift(
                    &store,
                    &[serde_json::json!({
                        "id": plan.module_id, "provides": provides, "src": src_rel
                    })],
                    by.as_deref(),
                    "module lift: the faithful module, not the preview derivative",
                )
            }
        })();
        match wrote {
            Ok(()) => lifted += 1,
            Err(e) => skipped.push(format!(
                "{rel} — the store REFUSED the write: {}",
                e.trim().lines().next().unwrap_or("").trim_start_matches("bsc: ")
            )),
        }
    }

    if !skipped.is_empty() {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("\nskipped {}:", skipped.len()));
        for s in &skipped {
            bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   {s}"));
        }
    }
    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
        "\n{lifted} component record(s) {}.",
        if apply { "lifted" } else { "would be lifted" }
    ));
    if !apply && lifted > 0 {
        bsc_util::emit_line("(dry run — pass --apply to write)");
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui shadow [--dry]` — the shadow-catalogue sweep. Ported from
/// `scripts/sync-shadow-catalogue.mjs`, which it replaces.
fn cmd_shadow(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let dry = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--dry");
    let repo = flag_after(args, "--repo")
        .map(std::path::PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or(std::env::current_dir().map_err(|e| format!("cannot resolve cwd: {e}"))?);
    let catalogue = repo.join("src/app/runtime/shadowPages.ts");
    let original = std::fs::read_to_string(&catalogue)
        .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", catalogue.display()))?;

    let (text, retired) = crate::shadow::sync(&original, |p| repo.join(p).is_file());

    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
        "{} graph-only: {}",
        if dry { "would declare" } else { "declared" },
        retired.len()
    ));
    for p in &retired {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   {p}"));
    }
    // WRITTEN WHENEVER THE TEXT MOVED, not whenever a retirement was found — the brace tidy-ups can be
    // the only change, and gating the write on the count made a re-run a no-op that reported success
    // while the glob stayed broken.
    if text == original {
        bsc_util::emit_line("   (catalogue already in sync)");
    } else if !dry {
        std::fs::write(&catalogue, text)
            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {}: {e}", catalogue.display()))?;
        bsc_util::emit_line("   catalogue updated");
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui retire <src-relative-path> [--dry]` — the deleter. Ported from `scripts/retire-module.mjs`.
fn cmd_retire(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    const USAGE: &str = "usage: bsc ui retire <src-relative-path> [--dry]";
    let dry = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--dry");
    let repo = flag_after(args, "--repo")
        .map(std::path::PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or(std::env::current_dir().map_err(|e| format!("cannot resolve cwd: {e}"))?);
    let repo_flag = flag_after(args, "--repo");
    let rel = args
        .iter()
        .find(|a| !a.starts_with("--") && repo_flag.as_ref() != Some(*a))
        .ok_or(USAGE)?
        .trim_end_matches('/')
        .to_string();
    // The argument is a SRC-RELATIVE PATH and is spelled the way a person has it in hand: with the
    // extension, and often with the `src/` the docs' own examples carry. Normalise both away before
    // anything derives a specifier from it — leaving them on produced `@/src/features/x/index.ts`.
    let rel = crate::retire::normalize_target(&rel);

    // A REAL LISTING, never `exists`: that is case-insensitive on Windows and would let a case-mismatched
    // path pass the very check meant to catch it.
    let files: Vec<String> = crate::retirable::list_src(&repo)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|f| f.ends_with(".ts") || f.ends_with(".tsx"))
        .collect();
    const EXT: [&str; 5] = ["", ".ts", ".tsx", "/index.ts", "/index.tsx"];
    let self_rel = EXT
        .iter()
        .map(|e| format!("{rel}{e}"))
        .find(|c| files.contains(c))
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("retire: no file at src/{rel} (tried .ts, .tsx and /index)"))?;
    // A BARREL IS ADDRESSED BY ITS DIRECTORY. `lib/plannerCore/index.ts` answers
    // `@/features/planner/lib/plannerCore`, never `…/plannerCore/index` — that is the specifier the
    // record actually `provides`. Emitting the `/index` form rewrote three importers onto a specifier
    // nothing answers, and typecheck caught it as TS2307 only after the file was already deleted.
    let rel_specifier = rel.strip_suffix("/index").unwrap_or(&rel).to_string();
    let spec = crate::retire::specifier_for(&rel);

    let seeds = crate::retirable::collect_seeds(&repo);
    let seed_source = seeds.get(&spec).map(|(_, _, src)| src.clone());
    let file_source =
        crate::record_source::file_as_record_source(&repo.join("src").join(&self_rel), &self_rel)
            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read src/{self_rel}: {e}"))?;
    let read = |p: &str| std::fs::read_to_string(p).unwrap_or_default();
    let exists = |p: &str| std::path::Path::new(p).is_file();
    let facts = crate::retire::RetireFacts {
        rel: &rel,
        spec: &spec,
        build_config_importers: crate::retire::build_config_importers(&repo, &self_rel),
        entry_importers: crate::record_source::entries_importing_statically(
            &repo.to_string_lossy(),
            &rel_specifier,
            &read,
            &exists,
        ),
        seed_source: seed_source.as_deref(),
        near_miss: crate::record_source::seed_answers_specifier(
            &spec,
            seeds.keys().map(|k| k.as_str()),
        )
        .1,
        file_source: &file_source,
    };
    // REFUSALS FIRST, before a single byte is written. Every one of them is a case where the file must
    // stay however good its record looks, and the message names the CONSEQUENCE rather than the rule.
    if let Some(r) = crate::retire::refusal(&facts) {
        eprintln!("{}", r.message(&rel));
        std::process::exit(1);
    }

    let rewrote = crate::retire::rewrite_importers(
        &repo,
        &files,
        &crate::retire::Target {
            self_rel: &self_rel,
            rel: &rel,
            specifier: &rel_specifier,
            spec: &spec,
        },
        dry,
        |f| {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   {}  {f}", if dry { "would rewrite" } else { "rewrote" }));
    });

    // The packaged SEED next: those are files in git, so this runs deterministically and needs no built
    // binary. It is a fence more than a sweep — `recordImports.test.ts` keeps the seed at zero relative
    // specifiers, so this should find nothing, and says so if it ever does.
    let mut seed_rewrote = 0usize;
    let seed_dir = repo.join("src-tauri/data/components/app");
    let mut seed_files: Vec<std::path::PathBuf> = Vec::new();
    fn walk_seed(dir: &std::path::Path, out: &mut Vec<std::path::PathBuf>) {
        let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else { return };
        for e in entries.flatten() {
            let p = e.path();
            if p.is_dir() {
                walk_seed(&p, out);
            } else if p.extension().and_then(|x| x.to_str()) == Some("json") {
                out.push(p);
            }
        }
    }
    walk_seed(&seed_dir, &mut seed_files);
    seed_files.sort();
    for f in &seed_files {
        let Ok(body) = std::fs::read_to_string(f) else { continue };
        let Ok(mut rec) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&body) else { continue };
        let (Some(src_text), Some(rec_src)) = (
            rec.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::to_string),
            rec.get("src").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::to_string),
        ) else {
            continue;
        };
        let hits: Vec<crate::record_source::RelSpec> =
            crate::record_source::relative_specifiers(&src_text)
                .into_iter()
                .filter(|r| crate::record_source::alias_for(&rec_src, &r.spec) == spec)
                .collect();
        if hits.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut text = src_text;
        for h in hits.into_iter().rev() {
            text.replace_range(h.at..h.at + h.spec.len(), &spec);
        }
        seed_rewrote += 1;
        let id = rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "   {}  seed record {id}",
            if dry { "would rewrite" } else { "rewrote" }
        ));
        if !dry {
            rec["srcText"] = serde_json::Value::String(text);
            if let Ok(out) = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rec) {
                let _ = std::fs::write(f, format!("{out}\n"));
            }
        }
    }

    let colocated = crate::retire::colocated_tests(&files, &rel);
    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("retire {rel}: {rewrote} importer(s) rewritten to {spec}"));
    bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   seed records: {seed_rewrote} rewritten"));
    // The live store, reported as part of the plan rather than left to a later command. Silence here is
    // the exact failure the sweep exists to undo, so a store that cannot be opened is REPORTED with the
    // command to run rather than swallowed or made fatal.
    match relative_specifier_summary(&flag_after(args, "--dir")) {
        Ok((sources, findings, ids)) => bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "   store: {sources} module sources · {findings} relative specifier(s) across {ids} record(s)"
        )),
        Err(e) => bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "   store: unreadable ({e}) — run `bsc ui imports --fix` once it is"
        )),
    }
    if !colocated.is_empty() {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "   KEEPING its colocated test: {} — it now tests the record",
            colocated.join(", ")
        ));
    }
    if dry {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   would delete src/{self_rel}"));
    } else {
        crate::retire::delete_module(&repo, &self_rel, &colocated)?;
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("   deleted src/{self_rel}"));
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Serializes every test that either SETS `$BSC_SCOPES` or drives a scope-GATED verb (`set` /
    /// `remove` on any collection): tests run in parallel threads sharing the process environment,
    /// so an unguarded scope test would make a concurrent mutation flakily refuse. Poisoning is
    /// ignored (an assert failure in one test must not cascade).
    static SCOPES_ENV_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());

    #[test]
    fn help_overview_lists_the_commands() {
        let ov = bsc_cli_util::help_overview("bsc ui", TAGLINE, COMMANDS);
        assert!(ov.contains("schema") && ov.contains("validate") && ov.contains("theme") && ov.contains("release"));
        assert!(ov.contains("emit-css"), "the #2489 emission verb is listed");
        assert!(ov.contains("generate"), "the #2634 palette generator is listed");
        assert!(ov.contains("resolve"), "the #2637 resolver/diagnostic is listed");
    }

    #[test]
    fn generate_produces_palettes_and_rejects_bad_shapes() {
        // happy paths — categorical / next / status all succeed and are pure output.
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into(), "categorical".into(), "--count".into(), "6".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into(), "categorical".into(), "--count".into(), "4".into(), "--seed".into(), "200".into(), "--pretty".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into(), "next".into(), "--existing".into(), "0,90,180".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into(), "next".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok(), "no --existing → the seed, still ok");
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into(), "status".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok(), "bare verb prints help");
        // bad shapes error crisply, never panic.
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into(), "categorical".into()], "bsc ui").is_err(), "missing --count");
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into(), "categorical".into(), "--count".into(), "x".into()], "bsc ui").is_err(), "non-numeric count");
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into(), "next".into(), "--existing".into(), "0,bad".into()], "bsc ui").is_err(), "bad hue");
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into(), "categorical".into(), "--count".into(), "2".into(), "--frob".into()], "bsc ui").is_err(), "unknown flag");
        assert!(run(vec!["generate".into(), "bogus".into()], "bsc ui").is_err(), "unknown subcommand");
    }

    // ── resolver + loud diagnostics (#2637) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    #[test]
    fn resolve_diagnostics_splits_theme_default_and_uncontracted() {
        use std::collections::HashSet;
        let contract: HashSet<String> = ["--card-bg", "--btn-border", "--fg"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
        let overrides: HashSet<String> = ["--card-bg"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
        let consumed = vec!["--card-bg".to_string(), "--btn-border".to_string(), "--nope-xyz".to_string()];
        let (misses, unc) = resolve_diagnostics(&consumed, &overrides, &contract);
        assert_eq!(misses, vec!["--btn-border"], "in contract but not the theme → default (a miss)");
        assert_eq!(unc, vec!["--nope-xyz"], "not in the contract → uncontracted (the loud gap)");
        // --card-bg is overridden by the theme → governed, in neither list.
    }

    }

    #[test]
    fn emit_css_prints_default_and_named_theme_and_writes_the_two_file_layout() {
        // stdout runs (default + named) succeed; the unknown id is a hard error listing the ids.
        assert!(run(vec!["emit-css".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok());

        let err = run(vec!["emit-css".into(), "--theme".into(), "nope".into()], "bsc ui").unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("unknown theme 'nope'") && err.contains("default"), "{err}");
        // Bad shapes error crisply.
        assert!(run(vec!["emit-css".into(), "--theme".into()], "bsc ui").is_err());
        assert!(run(vec!["emit-css".into(), "stray".into()], "bsc ui").is_err());
        assert!(run(vec!["emit-css".into(), "--frob".into()], "bsc ui").is_err());
        // --out writes the real two-file layout: tokens.css (the contract) + theme.css (the palette).
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-ui-emit-css-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        run(vec!["emit-css".into(), "--theme".into(), "nord".into(), "--out".into(), dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned()], "bsc ui").unwrap();
        let tokens = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("tokens.css")).unwrap();
        let theme = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("theme.css")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(tokens, crate::tokens_contract_css(), "tokens.css is the contract layer verbatim");
        assert!(theme.contains("theme: nord") && theme.contains("--bg-canvas: #2e3440;"), "theme.css carries the chosen theme's overrides");

    /// The CLI path end-to-end (#2800), against its OWN store.
    ///
    /// IT USED TO READ THE DEVELOPER'S LIVE LIBRARY (#3910). With no `--dir` it resolved the default
    /// `~/.base-studio-code/components/`, so the stamp it asserted was whichever kit that machine's `card`
    /// happened to belong to — the test passed or failed on LOCAL STATE rather than on the code, and it
    /// silently read the user's real library from a unit test. The stamp is not arbitrary: `cmd_emit`
    /// takes `from_store` when the store is NON-EMPTY and `packaged` when it is not, so the two paths
    /// stamp `bsc/studio` and `bsc/react-ui` respectively. Both are pinned below, which is what makes the
    /// assertion about the rule instead of about the machine.
    #[test]
    fn emit_component_writes_a_stamped_alias_free_closure() {
        let store = crate::test_store::SeededStore::new("emit-stamp");
        // ONE record, so the store is non-empty and the MERGED view is what emits. `card` itself still
        // comes from the packaged artifact underneath — this only selects the overlay path.
        store.seed(
            "unrelated-marker",
            r#"{"id":"unrelated-marker","name":"Marker","kitId":"base-studio-code","role":"composite","srcText":"export const marker = 1;\n"}"#,
        );
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-ui-emit-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        let d = dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        run(vec!["emit".into(), "component".into(), "card".into(), d.clone()], "bsc ui").unwrap();
        // Card landed mirroring the src/ layout, with NO first-party alias surviving, provenance-stamped.
        let card = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("shared/ui/data/Card.tsx")).expect("Card.tsx emitted");
        assert!(
            crate::emit::unvendored_aliases(&card).is_empty(),
            "emitted Card still IMPORTS {:?}",
            crate::emit::unvendored_aliases(&card),
        );
        // The stamp is `bsc/studio`, NOT the packaged kit's own id: since #3720 `emit` resolves against
        // the whole store, and an emitted cross-kit file did not come from `bsc/react-ui` (see
        // `EmitKit::from_store`, which sets the merged view's id). Do not "correct" this back — the
        // matching assertion in emit.rs expects the same id, and #4176 fixed this one for having been
        // left behind.
        assert!(card.starts_with("// vendored from bsc/studio@"), "provenance stamp: {card}");

        // ...AND THE OTHER PATH, which is what made the old assertion machine-dependent: with an EMPTY
        // store there is no merged view, `packaged` emits, and the stamp is the packaged kit's own id.
        // A fresh checkout hit exactly this and read it as a regression.
        let empty = crate::test_store::SeededStore::new("emit-stamp-empty");
        let dir2 = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-ui-emit-empty-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir2);
        run(
            vec!["emit".into(), "component".into(), "card".into(), dir2.to_string_lossy().into_owned()],
            "bsc ui",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let from_packaged =
            std::fs::read_to_string(dir2.join("shared/ui/data/Card.tsx")).expect("Card.tsx emitted");
        assert!(
            from_packaged.starts_with("// vendored from bsc/react-ui@"),
            "an EMPTY store emits from the packaged kit and stamps its id: {from_packaged}"
        );
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir2);
        drop(empty);
        // Command surface: bare emit prints help; bad shapes error crisply.
        assert!(run(vec!["emit".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok(), "bare emit prints help");
        assert!(run(vec!["emit".into(), "component".into(), "nope".into(), d], "bsc ui").is_err(), "unknown id");
        assert!(run(vec!["emit".into(), "kit".into()], "bsc ui").is_err(), "kit needs a dir");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
